newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria cenbank says still room for rate cut hopes.
newsitem.headline: Austria cenbank says still room for rate cut hopes.

text.p: Interest rates in Austria, while already at a historical low, may still have room to fall further, Austrian National Bank President Klaus Liebscher said on Wednesday.

"Room for movements has definitely narrowed but on the other hand there's always some room for hope," Liebscher told Reuters during an economic conference in this Tyrolean mountain village. "It's not clear whether the limit has been reached."

Rates in Austria fell to historic lows after the central bank last week followed the Bundesbank's lead and cut its securities repurchase rate to three percent from 3.20 percent, and its Gomex money market rate to 3.40 percent from 3.50 percent.
Liebscher added there was still a spread of 50 basis points between the money market rate and the key discount rate, which has been steady at 2.50 percent since April.
"The spread offers some leeway," he said without giving further details.

The central bank chief said he hoped for further rate reductions particularly at the longer end. "My hope would be that we'll see some reduction at the longer end. That would be very interesting for the economy," he said.

Liebscher's comments followed those of another senior central banker, National Bank director Adolf Wala, who on Monday said Austrian interest rates had reached a bottom and there was little, if any, room for further reductions. -- Knut Engelmann, Alpbach newsroom +43 5336 5597
